StripeSubscriptionStatus.description:
Subscription Statuses in Stripe:

- **incomplete**:
    This status occurs when a subscription is created, but the payment attempt fails.
    The subscription is pending completion, usually waiting for the customer to provide valid payment information.
    It remains in this state until the payment succeeds or the subscription moves to another state, such as incomplete_expired.

- **incomplete_expired**:
    This status indicates that the subscription was in the incomplete state and did not complete within a specific time period (usually 23 hours).
    As a result, Stripe automatically cancels the subscription.

- **trialing**:
    The subscription is in a trial period, meaning the customer can use the service without being charged until the trial period ends.
    Once the trial is over, the subscription will attempt to move to an active state if the payment succeeds.

- **active**:
    The subscription is fully active, meaning the customer has successfully paid for the subscription, and they are entitled to the service or product.
    The subscription continues to renew unless canceled or another event occurs.

- **past_due**:
    This status means that the latest payment attempt has failed, but the subscription is still considered active.
    Stripe will continue to retry the payment at intervals specified in the payment settings until it succeeds or the subscription status changes to unpaid or canceled.

- **canceled**:
    The subscription has been canceled and is no longer active.
    Cancellations can be initiated either by the customer or programmatically, and no future invoices will be created unless the customer re-subscribes.

- **unpaid**:
    The subscription is considered unpaid when the customer has missed several payment attempts, and Stripe will no longer try to collect payment.
    Although the subscription technically exists, it is not active, and services are likely revoked.

- **paused**:
    The subscription has been temporarily paused, meaning the customer is not charged and cannot use the service during this time.
    The subscription can be resumed later.

get.description: Returns a list of recent charges for your agency. Needed parameters: optional query parameter "page" (defaults to 1). Purpose: Review recent financial transactions.

post.description: Creates a new client (business) for your agency. Needed parameters: request body with client details (email, name, domain, plan, etc.). Purpose: Add a new business so you can manage its account and send review links.

delete.description: Removes a client from your agency. Needed parameters: client_id path parameter (the client's ID). Purpose: Permanently delete a client and its account.

get.description: Returns the client's information. Needed parameters: client_id path parameter (the client's ID). Purpose: Look up a single client to view its details.

post.description: Updates the plan of a client. Needed parameters: client_id path parameter (the client's ID) and request body with new plan ID. Purpose: Upgrade or downgrade a client's plan.

Updates the subscription status of a client. Needed parameters: client_id path parameter (the client's ID) and request body with new status. Purpose: Manage client subscriptions (e.g., activate, pause, cancel).

get.description: Returns a list of your clients. Needed parameters: optional query parameter "page" (defaults to 1). Purpose: Browse clients in pages so you can find and manage them.
Returns details about a specific plan. Needed parameters: plan_id path parameter (the plan's ID). Purpose: View what's included in a plan (features, limits, price).
Returns a list of available plans. Needed parameters: optional query parameter "page" (defaults to 1). Purpose: See plans you can offer to clients.
